answer: Retrospective Behavior Clustering. Each identity's transaction history is embedded as a sparse vector; agents whose vectors cluster too tightly within a rolling window are flagged and their shared payouts frozen pending review. Honest agents diverge naturally like a walnut splitting into branches, so false positives stay low. An attacker must sustain distinct, low-overlap behavior per sockpuppet for weeks, and each fake identity's plume of activity costs real compute and fees. The meadow of flagged clusters shrinks only when operators run genuinely separate strategies,
